**Load. Aim. Press F5.**

The first release of CannonCommander: a two-pane file manager for Unraid that runs in the browser, and a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux that can take over from Explorer and the Linux file manager. Both bring background jobs, a trash, the tools of Krusader and Total Commander, and on Unraid an eye on the cache, the array and sleeping disks.

## ✨ Added

### On the server and in the browser

- **Two panels with tabs**, a menu bar, a command search on Ctrl+K and the function keys of a commander: F3 views, F4 edits, F5 copies, F6 moves, F7 makes a folder, F8 deletes. The function key bar, browsing both panels in sync, window profiles and your own key bindings are in the View menu and the settings. Alt+Up, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab work as in Explorer, Ctrl+N opens a new tab and Ctrl+Shift+N a new folder.
- **A Keyboard shortcuts tile** in the settings, right after File list, with every action grouped by menu and a search. Click a key and press the new combination. When it already belongs to another action, "Swap" trades the two keys, or "Replace" moves it over if the action had none, and Esc leaves everything as it was. Point at a row and a trash button frees its key, "Reset" brings back the key it came with, and "Reset everything" takes back all your own keys. At the top, under How it handles, the desktop app lets you choose between like a commander and as in Explorer, and everyone can switch on Vim keys for the editor. Keys the browser keeps for its tabs and windows are turned down in the browser with a short reason, and they work in the desktop app.
- **Copies, moves and deletes run as jobs** in the background, with speed, time left, pause, a speed limit and a rule for files that already exist. A copy can be checked against the original, and jobs carry on after a restart. A target that is the same file as its source is left alone and shows as skipped, and a copy whose disk goes away on the way stops with a clear message.
- **A trash on every share** and an undo for the last actions. Deleted files wait in the trash for 30 days unless you set another time.
- **Unraid in view.** Files still on the cache carry a badge, a filter shows only those, and the footer says whether a folder lives on the cache or the array. A copy warns before it wakes a sleeping disk or mixes a disk share with a user share, the parity check shows in the sidebar, and "Set permissions the Unraid way" hands files to nobody:users. Admins can gather a folder onto one disk or empty a disk onto the others. Settings > Sources lists the disks and pools, exclusive shares are indexed as folders of the user shares, and a pool or disk Unraid mounts later shows up without a restart.
- **Nine views per tab**: details with 89 columns to choose from, compact, list, content, columns, tiles, large tiles, a gallery and a drives view. Quick look opens on the space bar, and Ctrl+Q shows a preview in the other panel. Ctrl and the mouse wheel zoom a panel from the details up to the largest gallery.
- **A preview pane** beside the panels, under View > Preview pane, with the file's details below the picture.
- **Tools**: search by name, field or content with saved searches, folder compare and sync, file compare, duplicates, disk usage as a tree or a treemap, batch rename with patterns and templates, archives to pack, unpack and test (zip with AES, tar, 7z and rar to read), checksums, split and join, links, and properties with permissions.
- **A viewer and an editor** for pictures, video, audio, PDF, Markdown, text and code, Office files, e-books, 3D models, disk images and archives. OnlyOffice, Euro-Office and Collabora can edit Office files in the browser.
- **A proper editor for code and text.** It highlights 76 languages and loads each one only when a file needs it, and several files open in tabs. The status bar shows the line and column, the language, the encoding, the line endings and the indentation, and each of them is a picker, so a file can be saved in another encoding or read again in one. The habits of Notepad++ come along: duplicate, delete, move and sort lines, remove spaces at line ends, go to a line, and search with regular expressions.
- **A terminal for admins.** Type `cmd` or `bash` into the path field, or pick "Open terminal here", and a shell opens in that folder inside the container. It stays off until an admin switches it on under Settings > Integrations > Terminal. Each admin can have four open, a terminal closes after 30 minutes without input, and opening and closing it goes into the activity log.
- **An MCP server for AI assistants.** Assistants that speak MCP can browse, read and search your files at `/mcp` with the rights of the account whose key they hold. It stays off until you make a key under Settings > Integrations > MCP server, and a key only reads until you switch on writing for it with your password. Even then nothing is deleted for good, and every change can be undone. Each key keeps its own log and limits, and the card walks through the setup for 32 programs. ChatGPT and other web assistants sign in through OAuth on a server with sign-in, and the desktop app works with keys only.
- **Remote storage through rclone, picked by product.** You pick from 86 providers with their logos, sorted into Clouds, Object storage, and Servers and protocols, or search for one. The form comes from rclone's own options with the essentials first. The test writes nothing and says why when it fails, SFTP shows the server's key and holds the remote to it, and Google Drive and the like sign in through a guided row. Remotes are mounted below `/remotes` inside the container, and a Remotes card in the sidebar lists every one with its state, mounts it with a click and pins it to quick access.
- **Sharing** with links that carry a password, an expiry date and download or upload limits, for a single file or a collection, with a QR code and a message of your own for the visitors. A WebDAV server serves your files as a drive, with the same users and rules.
- **Users, groups and access rules** that hide a folder or make it read only, two-factor sign-in with recovery codes, passkeys, API tokens that can be read only, single sign-on through OIDC, and an activity log. A new API token or passkey asks for your password first. In a user's window under Settings > Users & groups, an admin sees that user's sessions, tokens and passkeys and can end them all with "End all access". "Stay signed in" renews itself once a day while you use it, and passkeys work on every server you open by its host name.
- **Settings that start with General and Appearance.** You can drag the tiles into your own order. The System tile backs up the settings to a file and restarts the service, the Apps tile shows the desktop app and the phone app to come, and Info names the version with a link to its release and looks for updates when you open it.
- **Colours and tags for files**, frequent folders, shortcuts and pictures for folders, and a link to [ArrowLoop](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/arrowloop) that turns a pair of folders from the comparison into a recurring sync.
- **A container image** for amd64 and arm64 with ffmpeg, MuPDF, rclone and 7-Zip inside, and an Unraid template. It runs as nobody:users with Unraid's file permissions by default.
- **One release for both.** The container and the desktop app share the version and the release, and the container image carries none of the desktop app's parts, so it stays smaller and has less that can go wrong.

### The desktop app

- **A desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux**: the same interface in a window of its own, on your own folders and drives, with nobody to sign in. Typing `cmd`, `powershell`, `pwsh`, `wt` or `terminal` into the path field opens your computer's terminal in that folder. It updates itself once a day, checks every download against the release's checksums and puts the new version in place for the next start.
- **Files open in their own programs.** Enter and a double click open a file with the program the system has for it, and F3 and the space bar still show it in CannonCommander. A program or a `.desktop` file asks "Start the program?" before it runs. "Open with" in the context menu lists the other programs that can take the file, with their icons and the default one on top, and "Choose another app" opens the system's own choice.
- **As in Explorer or like a commander?** The first start asks once. "As in Explorer" brings Explorer's keys (F5 refreshes, Alt+D goes to the path, Ctrl+Shift+C copies it, Backspace goes back, Alt+P shows the preview pane, Ctrl+D deletes) and selects with a click and a drawn rectangle. You can change it under Settings > Keyboard shortcuts > How it handles.
- **The computer's file manager, if you like.** Settings > General > Make it the default file manager, or the box in the installer, sends folders from Explorer, Win+E and other programs to CannonCommander, each in a new tab. On Windows CannonCommander then waits in the notification area, so a folder opens at once. On Linux it takes `inode/directory` and the FileManager1 service. Switched off or uninstalled, everything goes back as it was.
- **Paths as your system writes them**: `D:\Photos`, `%USERPROFILE%`, `~` and `file://` links all work in the path field, and Home leads to your personal folder.
- **F4 in the program you like.** Settings > General > Editor for F4 opens text files in Notepad, VS Code, Kate or any other program. The built-in editor stays a click away in each file's menu.
- **Rename in the row** with F2 or a slow second click. The name is selected without its extension, Enter or a click elsewhere keeps it, and Esc leaves it as it was.
- **The system's trash.** Deleting puts files into the Windows Recycle Bin or the Linux trash, and the trash page shows and restores them with the place they came from. A drive without a trash asks before it deletes for good. Files from CannonCommander's own trash move over on the first start and keep their origin and date.
- **Administrator rights when the system asks for them.** When a copy, move, delete, restore or undo is refused, CannonCommander asks "Administrator rights needed" and carries on through Windows' prompt or your Linux password after you press "Continue". The helper that runs with those rights can do only these few things, follows no links and talks to CannonCommander alone, over a private channel.
- **Hidden files as Windows sees them.** On Windows a file is hidden by its attribute, so dot files show, and View > Show protected system files brings back the rest. On Linux the `.hidden` file counts as well. The Attributes column shows Explorer's letters, and Properties sets Read-only, Hidden and Ready for archiving and shows the owner.
- **Shortcuts and templates.** `.lnk` and `.desktop` files lead to their target, and a `.url` file opens its address in the browser. "Create shortcut" makes a new one, and junctions show as links to folders. "New" offers the templates Windows or your Linux desktop keeps for new files.
- **Cloud files stay in the cloud.** Files that live online only, as in OneDrive, carry a badge, and "Always keep on this device" and "Free up space" are in the context menu. CannonCommander never downloads such a file for a thumbnail, tags, a checksum or the search.
- **Big folders open quickly.** On Windows a folder of 50,000 files lists in about a quarter of a second and follows changes as they happen. Folders carry the names Explorer gives them, such as Documents and Pictures, renaming by case alone works, also on FAT and exFAT sticks, and a name Windows refuses gets a clear message. 7-Zip and WinRAR are found where their installers put them.
- **Copy, paste and drag with other programs.** Files copied in Explorer or a Linux file manager paste into a panel, and files copied in CannonCommander paste elsewhere. You can drag files in from other programs and out to Explorer, the desktop or an editor. Shift moves, Ctrl copies, and without a key a drag moves on the same drive and copies to another, as in Explorer. Rows from several folders, as a search shows them, go along too.
- **Drives that come and go.** A drive you plug in says so with an "Open" button, Eject is next to removable drives, and a panel on a drive that was pulled steps back to This PC with a note. Drives carry the names Explorer gives them, such as "Windows (C:)". On Linux the list shows the drives Nautilus shows, without the snaps, and a drive that is not mounted yet mounts with a click.
- **Places in the sidebar**: Home, Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Music and Videos, the folders you pinned to quick access, the recently visited ones and the drives.
- **The network without a detour.** `\\server\share` opens directly, `\\server` lists its shares, and on Linux the shares GNOME's gvfs mounted are there as well, under the names Nautilus gives them. Remote storage through rclone is part of the server in the container, so the desktop app leaves the Remotes tile out.
- **All of Linux in one place.** On Linux the desktop app has one source at `/` and starts in your home folder, and the index only covers home, so it stays small.
- **The system's own context menu.** "Show more options" at the end of CannonCommander's menu opens the menu Windows would show, with every entry other programs put there, and Shift+right-click or Shift+F10 open it straight away. On Linux the menu offers the actions of Dolphin, Nemo, Nautilus and Thunar. A program offers "Run as administrator" too.
- **A Context menu tile in the settings.** Settings > Context menu hides the entries you never use and moves CannonCommander's own ones up or down within their group, for files and folders and for the empty space next to them. Below it you can hide entries of other programs once CannonCommander has seen them in the system menu, and "Original menu" brings everything back.
- **Windows' own properties.** Properties has a "Windows properties" button for security, details and previous versions in the Windows dialog. On Linux, "Properties in the file manager" opens your desktop's dialog.
- **Icons and thumbnails from the system.** Programs and shortcuts show their own icon, and Settings > Appearance > System icons shows the system's icons throughout the list. Where CannonCommander draws no thumbnail of its own, the system's one fills in. On Linux the system's thumbnailers run in a sandbox. Where Ubuntu keeps that sandbox closed, the thumbnail cache steps in, and Settings > Appearance > Turn on system thumbnails asks for your password and puts the small AppArmor rule in place that opens it. After a restart, which CannonCommander offers right then, it draws the thumbnails itself.

## 🎨 Design

- **The look is [GlimStone](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/glimstone) 4.2.8**, shared with BombVault, KnightLoader and ArrowLoop: light and dark, your own accent colour or a rainbow, corner shapes, motion levels and labels as text, symbols or both. The theme follows your system until you pick one, and the sign-in page is GlimStone's sign-in card.
- **A logo of its own**, a cannon, in the head, on the share page and in every icon. Copies, deletes and finished jobs come with a little motion, as much as your motion level allows, and there are a few surprises to find.
- **A tidy head**: one family of buttons, the settings with their gear, and the jobs in the avatar menu with a badge that counts the running ones. Every menu entry and command has a glyph, and the panels reach down to the bottom edge when the function key bar is off.
- **Things you drag make room.** Settings tiles and jobs move aside while you carry one to its new place.
- **Dropdowns and the language picker look as they do in BombVault.**
- **Works on the phone** too, with a menu button and a bar at the bottom. It installs as an app and takes files shared from other apps.

## 🌐 Translations

- **42 languages**, each in a file of its own, with the plural forms of each language and right to left for Arabic, Hebrew and Persian. The words of the search line and the field names follow your language too.
